name: Glitch Sigmas (seeded multiplicative jitter)
plain: Takes a core schedule (karras, exponential, normal, simple or ddim_uniform, with the usual denoise tail crop) and multiplies every value by its own seeded random factor 1 + jitter·z. Only the last value is pinned back. The first sigma is jittered too, so the start can rise above the model's sigma_max. Nothing re-sorts the list, so at larger jitter the schedule can go up between steps, which some samplers treat as a restart. Interior values are clamped to at least 1e−6.
math:
Symbols: σ core schedule; j jitter; z_i ~ N(0,1) from a CPU generator seeded with seed.
σ'_i = max(σ_i·(1 + j·z_i), 1e−6) for i < N−1; σ'_{N−1} = σ_{N−1}.
